subject: MAP: Close timeline + hosting variance evaluation plan
messages:
From: John Park <john.park@acme.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + perf ask: hosting comparison (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Rachel / Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and infra teams want a short, concrete MAP that ties the commercial close to a small but high-fidelity performance validation before we commit to Dedicated. Key asks from ACME infra:

- Short evaluation that measures latency (p50/p95), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and behavior at target concurrencies (25, 50, 100 concurrent sessions).
- Compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for isolation and predictability under production-like bursts (10–20% traffic spikes).
- Observe autoscaling behavior and warm-start latency during scale-up events.

Can Redwood run the evaluation (with our test corpus) and provide: test plan, raw results, summary table for inclusion in procurement pack, and an updated MAP with a proposed close date contingent on results?

Attached is the current MAP draft from our side (ACME_MAP_v2.pdf). Ideally we get results and a sign-off window within two weeks so procurement can execute.

Thanks,
John
Director, Platform Engineering — ACME Corp
[Attachment: ACME_MAP_v2.pdf]

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + perf ask: hosting comparison (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

John —

Appreciate the clear asks. We can run a focused validation and fold outputs into an updated MAP. Proposed immediate actions:

1) Redwood test plan (attached): test matrix, dataset, measurement hooks, and run windows (we propose Wed-Fri this week). [Attachment: perf_test_plan_v1.xlsx]
2) Warm/cold start scenarios and autoscale triggers to reproduce your burst pattern.
3) Deliverables: CSV of raw traces, summary dashboard screenshots, 1-page MAP update and recommended hosting option by cost/perf tradeoff.

Quick question: can your infra team provide a short sample traffic trace (1 hour of representative RTs) or are we ok using the spike profile in the plan?

I’ve looped in Jordan (ops lead — will run the harness) and Karthik for architecture/quantization knobs. Marissa — can you advise on the MAP close language we should offer if numbers meet the bar?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: perf_test_plan_v1.xlsx]
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, John Park <john.park@acme.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + perf ask — test matrix and expected metrics

John / Rachel —

We built a compact test matrix that focuses on three key scenarios: steady-state (60 minutes), spike (sustained 10 min burst at +25% traffic), and scale-down window. For each hosting mode we will capture:
- P50 / P95 per-token latency (ms)
- TTFT median and 95th (ms) for 1k token generations
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency levels: 25 / 50 / 100 sessions
- Variability: standard deviation and 99th percentile over run window
- Autoscale reaction time: time from trigger to steady throughput (s)

Execution notes:
- Hosted: We will use the production routing policy and simulate burst using your trace. Expect some request-level queuing during scale events; we'll measure queuing delays.
- Dedicated: GPU pools pinned to the tenant — we expect best steady-throughput and lower variance.
- Private: depends on ACME infra profile; if on-prem with strict CPU/GPU isolation we expect similar to Dedicated; if VM oversubscription exists we may see noisy-neighbor variance.

Preliminary thresholds (for context) — not commitments:
- p95 per-token latency: Hosted < 120ms, Dedicated < 80ms, Private < 90ms
- TTFT (1k tokens): Hosted < 1.2s, Dedicated < 0.9s, Private < 1.0s

We'll instrument KV-cache hits and prefix caching effects; results attached will include raw traces.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, John Park <john.park@acme.com>, Nadia Lopez <nadia.lopez@starlite.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP perf runs — first-pass results attached

Team / John —

We completed the scheduled runs this morning. Attached is a condensed CSV and a 1-page summary. Highlights and interpretation below (full traces in redwood_perf_results_ACME.csv):

Summary table (median / p95):
- Hosted: p50 per-token latency = 48 ms; p95 = 118 ms; TTFT (1k tokens) median = 1.18 s; sustained throughput (100 concurrent sessions) = 6.2k tokens/sec; throughput stddev = 12%. Autoscale reaction from idle to steady = ~38s, queuing observed on the first 20s of the burst.
- Dedicated: p50 = 33 ms; p95 = 76 ms; TTFT median = 0.88 s; sustained throughput (100 concurrent) = 9.4k tokens/sec; throughput stddev = 4%. Autoscale (if configured) is effectively instant for pre-warmed pools; no queuing under the same burst profile.
- Private (ACME test infra — VM cluster): p50 = 36 ms; p95 = 102 ms; TTFT median = 0.95 s; sustained throughput (100 concurrent) = 8.1k tokens/sec; throughput stddev = 11%. We observed a noisy-neighbor incident on node-7 during run 2 that increased p95 by ~25% for a 7 minute window — resolved by isolating the job to a different host.

Interpretation: Dedicated provides the best latency, throughput, and predictability. Hosted meets SLAs for median latency but has higher tail events during initial autoscale windows. Private can be comparable when infra is appropriately provisioned and isolated; variability depends on ACME's node allocation and isolation.

Next steps we recommend:
- If ACME wants predictability for launch, Dedicated is the conservative choice.
- For cost-sensitive pilots, Hosted + a canary (2 week) with increased burst pre-warming and autoscale policy adjustments can work.
- If ACME plans Private, run a quick one-day isolation test post-provisioning to validate noisy-neighbor mitigation.

Files attached: redwood_perf_results_ACME.csv (raw traces) and a short summary screenshot (inline).

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_perf_results_ACME.csv]

1) Can Redwood reserve a small Dedicated pool for a 2-week canary (we need a predictable latency SLA during that period)?
2) Update the MAP so the procurement signer sees the outcome criteria and a proposed rollback path (if we hit noisy neighbor issues on Private).

Tentative procurement timeline: legal redlines by Sep 20, E2E sign-off Oct 1, target prod cutover Oct 15. If you can provide the updated MAP and a confirmation of the canary pool availability by Monday Sep 13 we can lock the timeline.

Best,
John

Rachel Kim
